title: How much does a Sikkim trip cost in 2026
meta_description: Indicative 2026 Sikkim trip costs per person: daily budgets for Gangtok, North and West Sikkim, package prices by tier, and where the money goes.
summary: A careful budget traveller can see Sikkim for about ₹1,800–2,500 per person per day in Gangtok and West Sikkim, and ₹2,500–3,500 a day in North Sikkim, where permits and vehicles push costs up. A Value trip with good hotels and a private car runs to about ₹4,000–6,500 a day, and Comfort trips start around ₹7,000–8,000.
key_takeaways: Budget travel in Gangtok and West Sikkim costs about ₹1,800–2,800 per person per day, twin sharing.
North Sikkim is the dearest region because every trip needs a registered vehicle and a permit, so plan on ₹2,500–3,500 a day even on a shoestring.
Our four-night Gangtok, Tsomgo and Nathu La trip starts at ₹11,500 per person on the Budget tier and ₹19,500 on the Value tier.
Vehicles, not rooms, are the biggest cost, so sharing a car or taking shared jeeps saves more than any hotel choice.

sections.heading: The short answer
paras: Sikkim is not an expensive state, but it is not as cheap as people expect either. The reason is geography. Almost every trip involves long drives on mountain roads, and the most famous sights, Tsomgo Lake, Nathu La, Yumthang and Gurudongmar, can only be reached in a registered vehicle with a permit. You cannot take a public bus to them. That one rule sets the floor for most budgets.

Rooms and food, on the other hand, are reasonable. A clean guesthouse double in Gangtok costs about ₹1,200–2,500 a night, and a meal in a local restaurant ₹200–450 a person. Shared jeeps between towns are cheap: ₹350–450 a seat from Siliguri to Gangtok, ₹400–500 to Pelling. If you travel the way local people do, you can keep the daily cost low and spend money only where the road demands it.

All figures in this post are indicative for 2026, per person, twin sharing, and drawn from the prices we use on our own journeys. They rise in April, May, October and the Christmas week, and fall in the monsoon and deep winter.

sections.heading: Daily costs by region and tier
paras: Every Go Sikkim Tours trip comes in three tiers. Budget means homestays and simple hotels with shared jeeps where possible. Value means good mid-range hotels and a private car. Comfort means the best rooms on the route and a private SUV throughout. The table shows what a day costs in each Sikkim region at each tier.

The ranges are wide because a day in Gangtok with a short taxi tour costs far less than a permit day to Nathu La. Use the lower end for rest days and town days, and the upper end for days with a long drive or a permit trip.

sections.heading: Where the money goes
paras: Transport is the largest single cost on almost every Sikkim trip. A reserved car from Siliguri to Gangtok costs ₹3,500–5,000, and from Bagdogra airport ₹4,000–5,500. A day trip from Gangtok to Tsomgo Lake and Baba Mandir costs ₹3,500–5,000 per car, or ₹5,500–7,500 with Nathu La. A reserved SUV for two nights in Lachung costs ₹14,000–19,000. Split between two people, those numbers dominate the budget. Split between five, they shrink fast.

Rooms come second. In Gangtok a guesthouse double is ₹1,200–2,500 a night. In Lachung a homestay room with meals is about ₹1,500–2,500 and a hotel with dinner and breakfast ₹3,000–6,000. West Sikkim has a wide spread, from family guesthouses in Upper Pelling to well-known resorts with Kangchenjunga views.

Food is the smallest item. A plate of momos or a bowl of thukpa costs ₹100–200 in most towns, and a full local meal ₹200–450. In North Sikkim meals are usually part of the package. Permit fees are small, typically a few hundred rupees, and are built into the vehicle or tour price.

sections.heading: How to spend less without missing the best parts
paras: The cheapest way to see Sikkim is to use shared transport on the long transfers and pay for a vehicle only where you must. That means a shared jeep from Siliguri to Gangtok, a pooled seat to Tsomgo, and a shared group tour to Lachung. Each of these saves thousands of rupees compared with a private car, and the experience is not much different.

Timing matters almost as much. March and November have good weather and lower prices than April, May and October, and you can often book North Sikkim a few days ahead at better rates. The monsoon is cheapest of all, but road closures make it a poor choice for permit areas.
list: Take shared jeeps for Siliguri to Gangtok, Gangtok to Ravangla and Pelling, and Pelling to Yuksom.
Book a pooled seat for Tsomgo and Baba Mandir at ₹700–1,200 rather than a whole car.
Choose the shared group tour for Lachung, the cheapest North Sikkim trip.
Stay in village homestays in Aritar, Zuluk, Lachung or Yuksom, where meals are usually included.
Eat in local momo shops and family restaurants rather than hotel dining rooms.
Travel in March or November rather than May or October.

sections.heading: Costs people forget to count
paras: Quotes for Sikkim trips usually cover rooms, the car and permits, but several smaller costs sit outside them. Together they can add ₹500–1,000 a day, so it is worth knowing them before you set a budget.
Cash matters too. ATMs work in Gangtok, Namchi and Pelling, but card payments and cash machines are scarce above Mangan, so draw enough money in Gangtok before a North Sikkim trip.
list: Airport and station transfers: ₹500–800 for a prepaid taxi from Bagdogra to Siliguri if you are taking a shared jeep onward.
Local taxis within Gangtok at ₹100–250 a trip, and a half-day sightseeing car at ₹1,800–3,000.
Room heaters in Lachung and Lachen, which some hotels charge for in winter.
The Zero Point add-on from Yumthang, about ₹3,000–4,500 per vehicle.
Snow boots and jacket hire on the way to Tsomgo or Yumthang, about ₹100–200 an item.
Monastery and museum entry fees, the Gangtok ropeway at ₹120–200, and tips for drivers.

sections.heading: Sample budgets for three kinds of trip
paras: A student pair on a six-night Gangtok and Lachung trip, using shared jeeps and a shared group tour, can manage on about ₹15,000–18,000 each, including the jeep from Siliguri, four nights in a Gangtok guesthouse, a pooled Tsomgo seat and the two-night Lachung tour. That leaves little room for extras but covers everything that matters.

A couple on a seven-night Value trip, with a private car for Gangtok, Tsomgo and Nathu La and a reserved car for Lachung, should plan for about ₹35,000–45,000 each. The car is the big line. Adding a second couple to share it brings the per-person cost down noticeably.

A family of four on a Comfort trip through Gangtok, Pelling and Ravangla, with the best rooms and a private SUV, will spend about ₹8,000–12,000 per person per day. Children sharing their parents' room bring the family total down, but vehicle costs stay the same.

Whatever the tier, keep one spare day in Gangtok for weather. Snow and landslides close the high roads for a day or more, and a spare day costs far less than a missed flight. Prices here are indicative. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: What is the cheapest way to visit Sikkim?
faqs.a: Travel by shared jeep from Siliguri to Gangtok for ₹350–450 a seat, stay in a guesthouse at ₹1,200–2,500 a room, take a pooled seat to Tsomgo Lake for ₹700–1,200, and join a shared group tour to Lachung for ₹5,000–7,500 including two nights' stay and meals. Eat in local restaurants and avoid April, May and October, when room and vehicle prices rise.

faqs.q: How much does a five-day Sikkim trip cost for two people?
faqs.a: On our Budget tier, a four-night Gangtok, Tsomgo, Nathu La and Rumtek trip costs ₹11,500 per person, so ₹23,000 for a couple. The Value tier is ₹19,500 per person and Comfort ₹34,000. These prices are indicative, twin sharing, and exclude travel to Bagdogra or NJP. Peak weeks around Durga Puja and Christmas can cost more.

faqs.q: Is North Sikkim more expensive than Gangtok?
faqs.a: Yes. Every North Sikkim trip needs a permit and a registered vehicle, and hotels in Lachung and Lachen are priced with meals. Budget travellers should plan on about ₹2,500–3,500 per person per day, against ₹1,800–2,500 in East Sikkim. The shared group tour to Lachung is the cheapest option, at ₹5,000–7,500 per person for two nights.

faqs.q: Do permit fees add much to the cost of a Sikkim trip?
faqs.a: Not much. Permit fees for Tsomgo, Nathu La, the Silk Route and North Sikkim are small, typically a few hundred rupees per person, and agents build them into the vehicle or package price. Foreign nationals' Inner Line Permit is free. The real cost of a permit area is the registered vehicle you must hire to reach it.

faqs.q: When is Sikkim cheapest to visit?
faqs.a: Rooms and cars are cheapest in the monsoon, from late June to early September, and in January and February. The monsoon brings landslides and permit suspensions, so it suits relaxed town stays more than high trips. For good weather at fair prices, March and November are the best value, with clear days and fewer holiday crowds than April, May or October.
